classification.difficultyReason: Apply the sine rule and its supplementary-angle solution to two supplied triangle configurations.

content.prompt: There are two triangles that have sides 9 cm and 5 cm. The angle opposite the 5 cm side is $22^{\circ}$. Find, in each case, the size of the angle opposite the 9 cm side, correct to the nearest degree.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 1, paired triangles beneath the stem
spec.description: Two triangles side by side, with horizontal bases and the same 22-degree left angle. Each upper-left side is labelled 9 cm and its opposite right side 5 cm. The left lower-right angle is obtuse; the right lower-right angle is acute. Ordinary source outlines and labels use house black.
spec.mathematics: The shared upper vertex is (9 cos 22°, 9 sin 22°). The two lower-right vertices are the intersections of the horizontal baseline with the circle of radius 5 centred at that upper vertex.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied side lengths and the 22-degree angles are visible; required angles are unlabelled.

answer.worked:
Let $\theta$ be the angle opposite the 9 cm side.
$$\begin{align*}
\frac{\sin\theta}{9}&=\frac{\sin22^{\circ}}{5}\\
\sin\theta&=\frac{9\sin22^{\circ}}{5}\\
\theta_1&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{9\sin22^{\circ}}{5}\right)\\
\theta_1&\approx42.3992^{\circ}\\
\theta_2&=180^{\circ}-\theta_1\\
\theta_2&\approx137.6008^{\circ}
\end{align*}$$
Both are valid because $22^{\circ}+137.6008^{\circ}<180^{\circ}$. To the nearest degree, the left triangle has angle $138^{\circ}$ and the right triangle has angle $42^{\circ}$.
